hotContext.criticalNews: Europe: FSD Supervised live in 5 small markets (NL/LT/EE/DK/BE) with 50M km driven; Italy application under review; Germany KBA test-vehicle trials expected to start. US: NTSB prelim clears software in Katy crash (driver override) but NHTSA EA26002 on 3.2M vehicles and Special Crash Investigation remain open. No new unsupervised FSD regulatory approvals this week. Tesla summer-2026 EU-wide mutual recognition still not delivered for major markets.

recentKeyChanges.title: Italy confirms Tesla FSD application under review via Dutch homologation recognition
recentKeyChanges.description: On or around July 13, 2026, Servedio Gaetano, General Director at Italy's Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport, confirmed on LinkedIn that Tesla 'only recently' submitted an application requesting recognition of the Dutch FSD homologation, and that the matter is 'in the analysis phase also based on the indications from the European community.' An Italian senator had previously urged prioritization after Netherlands approval. Critical read: this is an application receipt, not an approval. No timeline was given. Italy would be a major EU volume market if approved, but the fact that a large member state is still running a national analysis months after Dutch type approval undercuts Tesla's earlier claim that EU-wide mutual recognition would deliver broad summer-2026 access without repeating review. As of this week FSD Supervised remains live only in five EU countries: Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, and Belgium — none of which are top-tier European auto markets by volume.

positive_signals: Italian Ministry General Director publicly confirmed application received and under analysis
Path is mutual recognition of Dutch homologation — faster than a full de novo type approval
Review explicitly references European Community guidance, consistent with EU mutual-recognition framework
Italy would be the first large-population EU market if approved
negative_signals: Application only — no approval, no OTA activation, no go-live date
Confirms country-by-country process is still required despite mutual-recognition narrative
Tesla's anticipated summer 2026 EU-wide recognition has not delivered Italy (or Germany/France/Spain/UK)
Primary report is a LinkedIn exchange via Drive Tesla Canada; not yet corroborated by Teslarati/TeslaNorth/official Tesla IR

recentKeyChanges.title: FSD Supervised hits 50M km in Europe across five small markets; major markets still closed
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla announced that owners in the Netherlands, Estonia, Belgium, Lithuania, and Denmark have surpassed 50 million kilometres (~31 million miles) of FSD Supervised driving as of July 14, 2026 — roughly three months after the first EU approval (Netherlands, April 10). Uptake in approved markets is real and fast. Critical reality check: Europe's 50M km is ~0.26% of Tesla's ~12B global FSD miles, and the five live countries are small Baltic/Nordic/Benelux markets. Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the UK — the volume markets that matter for Robotaxi economics and FSD attach rates — still have no consumer FSD Supervised. Belgium (approved ~June 10) is now confirmed as the fifth European country, updating the prior 'Denmark = fourth' count. Mutual recognition is expanding, but slowly and only into secondary markets so far.

positive_signals: 50 million km driven in ~3 months since first EU approval — strong early adoption where legal
Five European countries now confirmed live: NL, LT, EE, DK, BE
Belgium activation completes fifth-country footprint via mutual recognition pathway
Company-announced milestone with multi-source coverage (TeslaNorth; referenced in 12B-mile follow-up)
negative_signals: 50M km is trivial vs ~12B global FSD miles — Europe remains a data rounding error
No major EU market (DE/FR/IT/ES) or UK has consumer FSD Supervised yet
Still Supervised Level 2 only — not unsupervised, not robotaxi-grade autonomy
Summer 2026 EU-wide recognition timeline from Tesla remains unproven as of mid-July
Country-by-country activation friction persists even after Dutch type approval

recentKeyChanges.title: FSD fleet hits 12 billion cumulative supervised miles; training data grows, software still on v14
recentKeyChanges.description: As of ~July 17, 2026 Tesla FSD (Supervised) fleet miles surpassed 12 billion globally, roughly one month after the 11 billion mark (June 9). Community tracking cited by TeslaNorth estimates 26–30 million new miles per day, with >4.5 billion of the total on city streets. Europe contributed 50M+ km across five small approved markets. Critical framing for the software roadmap: data volume continues to accelerate and feeds RL hard-example mining (explicitly referenced in v14.3.5 release notes for traffic lights, rare objects, animals). But cumulative miles are not a substitute for the delayed v15 10B-parameter architectural overhaul. Tesla has already stated current v14 is not safe enough for large-scale robotaxi expansion without 'major architectural improvements' — more supervised miles improve the current model but do not ship the next architecture. Metric is community-tracked, not an official Tesla IR disclosure.

positive_signals: 12B cumulative FSD Supervised miles (~1B added in ~5 weeks from 11B on June 9)
Daily accumulation estimated at 26–30M miles/day — rapid data flywheel
>4.5B miles on city streets — hardest domain for end-to-end driving
v14.3.5 release notes explicitly credit fleet-sourced hard RL examples for traffic lights, rare objects, animals
negative_signals: All 12B miles are Supervised (L2) — not unsupervised robotaxi miles
More data does not ship v15; architecture delay to late-2026/early-2027 remains the blocker
Community-tracked metric, not official Tesla IR audited disclosure
Musk previously admitted current stack needs major architectural improvements for scale safety
Europe's contribution (~50M km ≈ 31M miles) is a rounding error vs global total
